article.story: NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- — Trevor Lawrence has found a way to play even better, and he's elevating the Jacksonville offense right along with him. Lawrence threw for 352 yards and three touchdowns as the Jaguars beat the Tennessee Titans 40-23 on Sunday for their sixth victory in seven games. “I wouldn’t just say this is the best I’ve ever seen him,” Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington said. “I’m saying I always knew he could play at this level and, shoot, I feel like there’s more in the tank. And we all feel like that. So, I’m excited for him and he’s going to continue to keep balling.” The Jaguars (7-2) also won a franchise-record fifth straight against their AFC South rivals, and this was their eighth win in 11 games in the series. Jacksonville has a four-game lead sitting atop the division as well. Lawrence became the eighth-youngest in NFL history to reach 20,000 yards passing, at the age of 27 years and 40 days. “Can’t say enough about how he’s playing right now,” Jaguars coach Liam Coen said. He did it completing passes to nine Jaguars for the fourth-highest passing yardage total of his career. Lawrence has topped 300 yards passing in three of five games, and the Jaguars have scored at least 30 points in four straight games. That matches the franchise's longest such streak, first set in 2017 in Weeks 13-16. “I just have a lot of comfort in what we’re doing, a lot of confidence,” Lawrence said of his second season with Coen. “I know what we’re doing. I feel like myself and our whole offense, but myself and the staff, like we’re all on the same page. I know what we’re trying to get done.” Washington had a career-high 148 yards receiving by halftime and finished with 152. Cam Little kicked field goals of 46, 48, 36 and 40 yards. Bhayshul Tuten added a 6-yard TD run with 1:10 left, padding the score off Tennessee's turnover on downs. Travis Hunter had an interception as the Jaguars held Tennessee to 327 yards of total offense even with new trade acquisitions safety Jessie Bates III and defensive tackle Jordan Davis inactive. The depleted Titans (1-8) remain winless at home as they lost their fifth in their final season at Nissan Stadium. After trading their top two defensive players in tackle Jeffery Simmons and safety Amani Hooker, the Titans put two more on injured reserve Saturday in left guard Peter Skoronski and punter Tommy Townsend. Tennessee scratched three more starters, with rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate and linebackers Cody Barton and rookie Anthony Hill Jr. sidelined by injuries. Chandler Zavala, signed from the practice squad Saturday, started at left guard. “I thought our guys gave us everything they had,” Titans coach Robert Saleh said. “Unfortunately, they made more plays than we did.” The Jaguars took the lead from the opening drive and never trailed after Lawrence hit Washington for a 2-yard TD. Cam Ward found Elic Ayomanor for a 50-yard catch-and-run that was the longest completion of the quarterback's young career, and Ward capped the drive with a 2-yard TD pass to Daniel Bellinger, pulling the Titans within 13-10. Little's 36-yard field goal made it a 16-10 halftime lead. Joey Slye kicked two of his three field goals in the second half to keep the Titans within range. Jacksonville answered with a 10-play drive, capped by a 3-yard TD pass by Lawrence to Brenton Strange on fourth-and-2 at the Titans 3. Saleh was furious officials missed a pick on his defender, leaving Strange wide open for the TD catch and a 23-13 lead. Lawrence made it 30-16 with a 25-yard TD pass to Josh Cameron early in the fourth quarter. The Titans answered with Tony Pollard taking a dump-off pass from Ward 32 yards to the end zone pulling them within 30-23 with 8:21 remaining. That was as close as they would get. Injuries Jaguars DE Danny Striggow was evaluated for a concussion in the first half and did not return. Jaguars C Robert Hainsey hurt his left knee early in the third quarter and did not return. Titans S Tony Adams suffered a concussion that sidelined him, and WR Wan'Dale Robinson hurt an ankle. Up next The Jaguars visit the New York Giants. The Titans visit Dallas. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here
